This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Root eighths**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

The root on every eighth note, the beats a little louder: the rock bass line under With or Without You and a thousand others.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root eighths","opts":{"bassFeel":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-halves.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Roots on every beat

The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-roots.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Root eighths, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Eight even roots a bar, a little heavier on the beats. On bass, alternate two fingers or use downstrokes with a pick, and mute with the fretting hand between notes so they do not blur. Lock with the kick drum: the beats are where it lands.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root eighths","opts":{"bassFeel":"eighths"}},{"label":"Roots on every beat (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root eighths","opts":{"bassFeel":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root eighths","opts":{"bassFeel":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## In other styles

The same bass line in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.
